claims.explanation: Ouabain is a cardiac glycoside that binds and inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on specific ATP1A1/ATP1B isoform expression and on HIF-1alpha-driven survival signaling, since cardiac glycosides block HIF-1alpha synthesis and HIF-1-dependent tumor growth. Lines with high ATP1A1 (and/or ATP1B1) expression, or with HIF-1 pathway activation, should be more sensitive, whereas lines with low pump expression or compensatory ouabain-resistant transport would be protected.

features.basis: primary ouabain target; higher expression increases binding and pump inhibition
beta-subunit required for functional Na/K-ATPase; modulates ouabain affinity
cardiac glycosides inhibit HIF-1alpha synthesis; HIF-1-dependent lines are more sensitive
VHL loss stabilizes HIF-1alpha, creating dependence on HIF-1 that ouabain blocks
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, suggesting p53 loss lowers apoptotic threshold
KRAS-mutant pancreatic/lung lines are enriched among sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid lines appear in the sensitive set
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and appears in several sensitive lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling and appears in sensitive lines
STK11-mutant lung lines are enriched among least-affected lines
KEAP1-mutant lines appear among least-affected lines, suggesting NRF2-driven protection
NF2-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected lines
